correctness.rationale: For every approval profile a>0, a disapproving coalition S with shared better set T has size ≤h_T, while coalition H_T proves the converse, so blocking iff some subset T has m h_T>a(m−|T|). With m fixed, independent Bernoulli bits give h_T/n→(1−p)q^|T| and a/n→p; maximizing q^k/(m−k) over k∈[0,m−1] follows from positive second derivative of k log q−log(m−k), leaving only k=0 or k=m−1. Hoeffding controls strict off-boundary margins. At a single-front threshold a nondegenerate one-dimensional CLT yields 1/2. At the simultaneous front, Y=approval of c and Z=disapproval with approval of every rival are mutually exclusive with P(Y)=1/2,P(Z)=1/(2m). For U=Y−1/2 and V=Y−mZ, Var U=1/4, Var V=(m+1)/2, Cov=1/2, giving rho=sqrt(2/(m+1)); the Gaussian quadrant formula gives the critical limit. The a=0 convention is exponentially negligible for p>0 but included exactly. Independent direct and reduced veto definitions agreed on 8448 binary profiles; covariance was recalculated algebraically for m=2..11. The infinite limit is proved by LLN/CLT, not by simulation.

final_claim: For fixed candidate number m≥2, i.i.d. independent binary approvals with distinguished approval probability p and common rival approval probability q yield an exact finite AWVC coalition-blocking subset test and the asymptotic survival phase p*=max(1/2,mq^(m−1)/(1+mq^(m−1))). At the two-front boundary p=1/2,q=m^(−1/(m−1)), the Gaussian quadrant survival limit is 1/4+arcsin(sqrt(2/(m+1)))/(2π), equal to 3/8 at m=3.
limitations: Fixed finite m, i.i.d. independent approval bits, distinguished probability p and common rival q.
No joint dependence across different target candidates; no growing-m or correlated approval phase, no finite-n exact probability claimed.
